citationText: A. Choudhury and S. Daly, “Combining Quality Metrics for Improved HDR Image Quality Assessment,” Proc. IEEE Conf. Multimedia Inf. Process. Retrieval (MIPR), pp. 179–184, 2019. Conclusion In this study, we investigated the suitability of objective quality metrics for compressed HDR/WCG images encoded with HLG. Our main findings are three. First, the chroma components must be taken into account by objective metrics, because HDR metrics that consider only the luminance channel fail to detect color distortions that observers can notice; second, the results of the investigated metrics that do consider color are nonetheless worse than the results of VIF, despite the fact that VIF is applied only on the luminance; and third, each color difference metric behaves differently depending on the type of the test image. Based on these results, as future work, we will study the aggregation of metrics into a single one as a solution to the open problem of finding an objective metric for HLG-encoded HDR/WCG content.
title: Combining Quality Metrics for Improved HDR Image Quality Assessment
